findings.title: Retry binding silently redefines the existing v1 chain and invalidates append-only R01 history
findings.reproduction: Candidate 3680ecf86f455b8cbd6a10c27b63ae62c836e359 writes segment_key='rfc8785.sha256.v1' and computes each chain hash over previous-chain, record_sha256, and sequence. Candidate 7dad75557cce78a905c6e97a4fd5dc43ee8e393a adds idempotency_sha256 to that material but leaves _PROVENANCE_SEGMENT_KEY unchanged. Materialize one exact valid R01 row (the schema and every stored column are unchanged), retain its original chain/checkpoint hash, and open it with R02. _ledger_integrity_state recomputes only the new formula and returns integrity-review, even though canonical bytes, record hash, event/project projections, normalized children, narrow audit, stored retry fingerprint, and the exact R01 checkpoint are mutually consistent; read-only lineage items remain visible. Appending under R02 continues the mixed formula under the same segment. This contradicts ADR-0024 and docs/architecture/provenance-contracts.md, which require a hash-algorithm/material change to start a declared new segment and never rehash or invalidate prior events in place.
findings.required_remediation: Preserve the exact R01 v1 formula and bind retry authority without redefining that segment, or introduce a declared v2 segment with a distinct key and version-dispatched verification while retaining exact read/verification support for v1. New writes after an existing v1 tail must transition deterministically without rewriting it, and each segment chain must start and verify under its declared formula. Add a fixture produced by exact R01 code, open and verify it under the remediation, append a new event, restart, and prove both historical and new segments remain verified. Keep a negative case for a fingerprint rewrite under whichever bound authority is selected.

findings.title: Mutable outbox and narrow-audit authority remain outside the verified transaction binding
findings.reproduction: Commit aggregate A with key A and aggregate B with key B. Update only outbox A's revision_id to B's valid same-project revision; no ledger, checkpoint, canonical record, normalized projection, narrow audit, fingerprint, or append-only trigger changes are required because outbox authority columns are currently mutable. Retry the exact A draft/event/key. _replay joins ledger A by record hash and confirms A's stored fingerprint, then returns _by_revision_id(outbox.revision_id), so it returns aggregate B. Lineage for A still reports verified because _ledger_integrity_state does not inspect outbox authority. Independently, rewrite only the narrow provenance_events.actor_type from human to model or its trace_id while restoring the exact append-only triggers; both pages remain verified. R02 compares narrow actor_id but not actor_type or trace_id even though the canonical event binds agentType and traceparent. Thus exact retry is not guaranteed to return the prior canonical result, and a supposedly verified atomic audit can contradict two material actor/trace facts.
findings.required_remediation: Fail closed unless an idempotency replay's outbox project, revision, event type, time, key, and record digest bind to the same canonical ledger event/output and narrow audit transaction before returning a projection. Protect outbox authority columns from delivery-state updates, or validate every authority field at replay and integrity boundaries while permitting only the intended dispatch-state transition. Compare narrow actor_type and trace_id to the canonical agent type and traceparent, in addition to the already checked identity fields. Add restart tests that mutate each outbox authority independently and prove no wrong projection can replay, plus restored-trigger actor-type and trace-id corruptions that must produce bounded integrity-review.
